repository_resolution: The native Mise lock binds eleven native tools with macOS arm64 records, nine of which also have Linux x64 records; Prettier retains its portable npm sidecar. The hosted publication job selects nine locked tools, Typst included; the earlier six-tool publication qualification remains dated evidence. The four CI records were added through a scoped native lock without changing existing tool records or npm sidecars. Native tasks install nothing; the isolated CI bootstrap installs only its selected locked tools under job-local build/runtime/ci. Independent-machine PDF bootstrap remains unqualified. Poppler has a qualified Homebrew Bundle declaration/check/execution binding described in pdf_inspection, not an exact-version lock. Homebrew remains the host installation owner.

font_supply.typst: Songti SC and Charter from macOS; Noto Sans CJK SC from its existing Homebrew cask; DejaVu Sans Mono and Libertinus Serif embedded in Typst 0.15.1 (Libertinus as the declared fallback for symbols in code that neither code face holds); Apple Color Emoji from macOS as the observed emoji fallback.
font_supply.figures: publication/layout/figures.typ sets every figure's labels in Noto Sans CJK SC; Typst draws the figures in the book's compile from the same font supply.
font_supply.closure: The bound replay checks six actual font files, the exact compiler with its embedded fonts, and all ten complete package roots through publication/supply/typst-inputs.sha256. Typst inputs.json still omits font reads. Same-host, network-disabled replay equalled the delivered PDF byte-for-byte for the editions qualified on 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11; a replay of an edition whose figures are drawn in Typst, extra supplied files and second-machine reproduction remain unqualified.
font_supply.rights: No standalone font binaries are included in repository source. Delivered PDFs embed used font faces; each font retains its own terms. See publication/rights/third-party-notices.md.

pdf_inspection.locked_repository_resolution: publication/brewfile declares Poppler. The native pdf-tool task checks the installed bundle and executes commands through brew bundle exec; pdf-tools-check verifies pdfinfo and pdftotext and gates test and bootstrap. This binding and the native check pass on the authoring host without installation or upgrade. The Brewfile does not lock the exact package version; independent-machine bootstrap remains unqualified.

reproduction: The source avoids private machine bindings, but the current layout depends on macOS font supply and has not qualified a second-machine build. Matching compiler, actual font files, complete resolved packages, diagram sources and fixed document date are reproduction prerequisites, not a byte-identical guarantee; replaying an edition whose figures were PNG images also needs that edition's frozen images. A font substitution requires relayout and successor acceptance.
